label: input x late in the original phase, in sequences starting with s/n/v
explanation: Fires almost only when the input token is x during the original phase at positions 5-8, usually the last 1-3 tokens before <DEL> (91% of activation mass is on x inputs, none in the copy phase). Small leftover activations fall on the token right after such an x and on <DEL>. Only about 6% of late-position x inputs activate it, so the prefix matters: sequences starting with s, n or v (and to a lesser degree a/w/i, or ones containing z, s, n, f, r) are strongly enriched, and the strongest activations come from such sequences. No crisp context rule was found. Adding first_tok in {s,n,v} raises precision to about 0.30 but cuts recall to about 0.40, so the context dependence looks distributed through the hidden state. It does not fire on x at positions 0-3, on non-x tokens (apart from that small spillover), or anywhere in the copy phase.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=s (+4.99), orig0=n (+4.17), orig0=v (+3.83), orig2=z (+3.74), orig1=n (+3.53), prev_tok=f (+3.04). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.86), prev3_tok=- (-3.62), phase=2 (-3.19), t=3 (-3.00).
